final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor introduced no genuinely new admissible evidence and largely reframed the same record more narrowly. That reframing is directionally more accurate than clean certification: it correctly concedes that aggregate readiness and rehearsal results support only a limited operational-readiness argument, not satisfaction of the internal release policy. But the crucial compliance predicates remain unmet on the admissible record. The evidence still shows a 1.2 percentage point gap in a named launch use case tied to customer commitments, an open legal disclosure review, and a policy requiring material limitations for named launch use cases to be resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. No new evidence closes any initial concern. A caveated description of weakness may be more precise as characterization, but it is not itself evidence that the policy condition was satisfied. For that reason, the record remains noncompliant rather than compliant_with_caveats.
remaining_concerns: The telehealth discharge planning segment still misses target and remains a named launch use case tied to two clinic network commitments.
The governing policy still treats this weakness as material because it affects a named launch use case and customer commitments; the product 'non-core' note does not resolve materiality.
No admissible evidence shows the policy predicate was satisfied before launch by resolution of the gap, disclosure of the material limitation, or approved risk acceptance.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required is still open, so the disclosure question remains unresolved on the record.

Aggregate readiness clearance, lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents, and public risk-management guidance do not by themselves satisfy the specific internal policy requirement for a material named launch use case.
